meta.name: Landing Page Bounce Check
meta.description: Calculates the bounce rate of every page visitors land on first, so you can fix the entrances that lose the most visitors

msg.welcome:
Hello. This is the **Landing Page Bounce Check**.
It looks for entrances where visitors arrive and leave straight away.
msg.ask_period:
Choose the period and the minimum number of visits to include.
Pages with very few visits swing wildly and will mislead you.
msg.result_head: Done. Here is the site-wide picture first.
msg.table_intro:
Bounce rate per landing page. Start with the **red rows**.
Click a row to see the diagnosis and what to do about that page.
msg.pick_row: Click a row you care about, or change the conditions and run it again.
msg.next: What would you like to do next?
msg.no_data:
There is no visit data for this period.
Please try a different period.
msg.no_match:
No landing page reached the minimum number of visits ({$min_sessions}).
Lower the minimum or widen the period.
msg.error:
Something went wrong while fetching the data.
Please wait a moment and try again.

cal.site_bad:
The site-wide bounce rate is **{$site_bounce_rate|percentage}**, which is high. What your entrances offer may not match what visitors expected.
Start with **{$worst_title}** ({$worst_rate|percentage}).
cal.site_mid:
The site-wide bounce rate is **{$site_bounce_rate|percentage}** - a common level.
Still, **{$high_count|integer} page(s)** are above 70%. Check **{$worst_title}** first.
cal.site_good:
The site-wide bounce rate is **{$site_bounce_rate|percentage}**, which is healthy.
At this level the remaining upside is page by page. Look only at the high rows below.
cal.detail_numbers:
Visits **{$selected_sessions|integer}** / bounces **{$selected_bounces|integer}** / bounce rate **{$selected_rate|percentage}**
This entrance collects **{$selected_share|percentage}** of all visits to the site.

adv.urgent:
Many visits and a high bounce rate means the **absolute number of visitors lost here is large**. Fixing this page pays off quickly.

What to check, in order:
1. Does the wording of the search result or ad match the heading at the top of the page?
2. Does the first screen (before scrolling) make clear what can be done here?
3. Is there a link or button to the next step within that first screen?
adv.bad:
The bounce rate here is **{$selected_rate|percentage}**, which is high. Visits are still modest, so this is the stage for forming a hypothesis.

Check whether the heading of this page matches what the traffic source promised.
adv.mid:
A bounce rate of **{$selected_rate|percentage}** is within the usual range.
For a page people read and leave satisfied (an article or a glossary entry) this is fine. If you want visitors to move on, revisit where the next-step link sits.
adv.good:
A bounce rate of **{$selected_rate|percentage}** is healthy. This entrance guides visitors onward well.
Consider reusing its heading and navigation pattern on the entrances that bounce hardest.
